assertions.description: Treats a GHCR authentication or push failure as a Phase 4 problem and never pushes the build to Docker Hub

assertions.name: normalizes-ghcr-namespace
assertions.description: Uses the lower-case current GitHub login in the GHCR repository path

assertions.name: builds-linux-amd64
assertions.description: Builds the exact Phase 3 plan for linux/amd64

assertions.name: records-buildx-digest-and-pull-access
assertions.description: Persists the digest from the same Buildx push plus anonymous, ghcr_secret_required, or indeterminate pull_access in build-result.json

evals.prompt: Deploy a Compose project whose README and Compose file declare public Docker Hub images acme/frontend:v2 and postgres:16. Both exact selectors resolve to immutable digests, every final workload is covered, and gh is not installed.
evals.expected_output: Phase 2 reuses both project-declared Docker Hub images by immutable digest, preserves the application and database topology, and skips Phases 3 and 4. Missing gh is only a path-specific warning and does not block this deployment because no local image must be pushed

assertions.name: reuses-declared-docker-hub-images
assertions.description: Keeps explicitly declared Docker Hub application and database images when their selectors resolve to digests

assertions.name: does-not-confuse-reuse-with-push
assertions.description: The GHCR-only Phase 4 upload policy does not remove Phase 2 Docker Hub image discovery or reuse

assertions.name: preserves-complete-topology
assertions.description: Carries both the frontend and PostgreSQL workload into template generation

assertions.name: skips-local-build
assertions.description: Skips Phases 3 and 4 because every final container workload already has an immutable image

assertions.name: does-not-require-gh-without-build
assertions.description: Does not block on missing gh when no local build/push path is needed

evals.prompt: Update an existing version 1.1 deployment whose state maps frontend to Deployment/shop container web and worker to StatefulSet/shop-worker container worker. Both services changed and have independent build plans. Both GHCR builds succeed, frontend becomes ready, but worker rollout fails.
evals.expected_output: The update builds both selected services for linux/amd64 and records their GHCR digests before mutating the cluster. It updates the exact recorded workload/container targets rather than guessing from the app name. When the worker rollout fails, it restores both frontend and worker to their previous digests, keeps the current per-service state unchanged, and appends target-qualified failure history

assertions.name: uses-per-service-build-plans
assertions.description: Builds frontend and worker with their own context, Dockerfile, target, and argument names

assertions.name: pushes-every-new-image-to-ghcr
assertions.description: Uses GHCR for both new update images with no registry prompt or fallback

assertions.name: targets-recorded-workloads
assertions.description: Uses Deployment/shop:web and StatefulSet/shop-worker:worker rather than deriving a target from app_name

assertions.name: mutates-only-after-all-builds
assertions.description: Does not change a live workload until every selected service build succeeds

assertions.name: rolls-back-the-whole-update-set
assertions.description: Restores every target changed in this operation when one selected rollout fails

assertions.name: preserves-current-state-on-failure
assertions.description: Does not partially advance services[].image, pull_access, or the primary image summary

assertions.name: records-target-qualified-history
assertions.description: Failure history identifies service, workload kind/name, container, previous image, and attempted image

evals.prompt: Update a multi-service deployment. An unchanged private worker still uses ghcr.io/account-a/worker@sha256:<digest>, while the current active GitHub account builds a private api image under ghcr.io/account-b/api@sha256:<digest>.
evals.expected_output: Before changing any cloud resource, the update evaluates the complete prospective service inventory and refuses to overwrite the app-scoped GHCR credential because its non-anonymous images span two namespaces. It asks the user to rebuild every conflicting private or indeterminate service under one GitHub account; it does not partially update workloads or state

assertions.name: checks-complete-service-inventory
assertions.description: Includes unchanged services when determining which GHCR credential the application still needs

assertions.name: requires-one-private-namespace
assertions.description: Allows only one normalized GHCR namespace across ghcr_secret_required and indeterminate service images

assertions.name: stops-before-cluster-mutation
assertions.description: Does not refresh the Secret, patch imagePullSecrets, or set a workload image when namespaces conflict

assertions.name: does-not-overwrite-another-account
assertions.description: Never replaces account-a credentials with account-b credentials while an unchanged private account-a image remains in use

assertions.name: preserves-state
assertions.description: Leaves the per-service state and history unchanged because no update operation began

evals.prompt: Generate Phase 5 for a Compose project where worker is declared first, api exposes only port 8080, and frontend publishes port 3000 with API_URL=http://api:8080. Phase 4 reports frontend as ghcr_secret_required and worker as anonymous.
evals.expected_output: Phase 5 selects frontend as the sole public service regardless of declaration order, preserves api as an internal Service, rewrites frontend's API URL to the generated api Service FQDN, injects the app-scoped pull Secret only into frontend, writes .sealos/template/index.yaml, and passes the complete quality gate

assertions.name: selects-public-service-by-contract
assertions.description: Uses frontend as the public workload and Ingress backend because it is the sole application service publishing Compose ports

assertions.name: preserves-internal-expose-port
assertions.description: Creates an internal api Service on port 8080 from Compose expose without creating an api Ingress

assertions.name: rewrites-internal-service-url
assertions.description: Maps http://api:8080 to the generated api Service FQDN using the Sealos namespace variable

assertions.name: scopes-private-pull-secret
assertions.description: Adds imagePullSecrets with the app-scoped name only to frontend and omits it from the anonymous worker and reused services

assertions.name: validates-canonical-artifact
assertions.description: Runs the complete quality gate against .sealos/template/index.yaml and does not fail R013 on the canonical deploy path

evals.prompt: Deploy a GitHub repository from a temporary checkout through the Template API. The kubeconfig selects namespace ns-demo, the built image is private GHCR, the API returns a random instance name, and the workload becomes ready after creation.
evals.expected_output: Phase 6 resolves and validates ns-demo before any Secret operation, performs the dry-run and real request with the same template and args, creates the app-scoped GHCR pull Secret for the returned instance, waits for every workload and public Service endpoint before Phase 6.5, validates state.json, persists the validated state outside the temporary checkout, and only then removes the checkout

assertions.name: initializes-namespace-before-secret
assertions.description: Reads and validates the kubeconfig namespace before Template API submission and passes that exact namespace to the pull-Secret helper

assertions.name: uses-identical-dry-run-and-create-inputs
assertions.description: Sends the same template bytes and argument object to dry-run and the real create request

assertions.name: materializes-secret-after-random-name
assertions.description: Explicitly assigns APP_NAME from the allowlisted DEPLOY_RESULT.response.name, validates it as a Kubernetes name, and uses that exact value for the app-scoped Secret without guessing

assertions.name: runs-common-readiness-gate
assertions.description: Waits for every returned or rendered workload and for public Service endpoints before runtime truth

assertions.name: persists-state-before-cleanup
assertions.description: Validates state.json, copies it to the stable GitHub repository state bridge, and cleans the temporary checkout only after persistence succeeds

evals.prompt: Deploy a repository with no root Compose file. Its parent Helm Chart defines API, UI, registry, and worker Deployments, their Services and Ingresses, RBAC, and one PostgreSQL KubeBlocks Cluster. The repository CI contains independent build plans for the four application images.
evals.expected_output: Phase 2 selects the parent Helm Chart instead of the implicit single-service fallback, renders it from a temporary copy without installing it, inventories the complete topology, resolves or builds each application image independently, and Phase 5 converts the rendered Kubernetes resources into one validated Sealos template without dropping the database, worker, registry, RBAC, or internal/public URL wiring

assertions.name: selects-explicit-helm-source
assertions.description: Selects the parent Helm Chart as deployment_source.kind=helm and does not treat vendored dependency Charts as independent sources

assertions.name: renders-without-installing
assertions.description: Uses a temporary Chart copy, rebuilds declared dependencies when needed, runs helm template without hooks, and never runs helm install or mutates the source Chart

assertions.name: does-not-fallback-to-single-service
assertions.description: Keeps all explicit Helm resources and never creates the implicit single-application service

assertions.name: matches-build-plans-per-container
assertions.description: Binds each CI build context, Dockerfile, target, and build-argument-name list to the matching workload/container service key

assertions.name: preserves-complete-topology
assertions.description: Retains API, UI, registry, worker, Services, Ingresses, RBAC, and the PostgreSQL KubeBlocks Cluster or an explicitly mapped equivalent

assertions.name: pins-every-workload-image
assertions.description: Uses a distinct immutable digest override for every emitted container workload rather than one top-level image for all services

assertions.name: normalizes-runtime-references
assertions.description: Binds RoleBinding ServiceAccounts to the selected Sealos namespace and rewrites application URLs to the generated Service or Ingress identities

assertions.name: accounts-for-every-source-resource
assertions.description: Writes a source resource mapping and topology evidence in which every rendered resource is preserved, transformed, or explicitly filtered exactly once

assertions.name: validates-template-and-topology
assertions.description: Runs the complete docker-to-sealos quality gate against both the canonical template and topology evidence before deployment

evals.prompt: Run Phase 1 for https://github.com/fanux/sealos-brain-homepage, a static HTML/CSS/JavaScript project served by Nginx. It has no package manager or language runtime version, and its existing Dockerfile exposes the application on port 3000. Continue the deployment lifecycle.
evals.expected_output: Phase 1 records the static project facts without coercing them into a known backend stack: language html, all_languages containing html/css/javascript, framework nginx, package_manager null, port 3000, and an empty or null runtime_version. The analysis artifact validates and the lifecycle continues to Phase 1.5

assertions.name: accepts-open-language-values
assertions.description: Treats html, css, and javascript as valid descriptive language facts rather than rejecting them against the deterministic detector vocabulary

assertions.name: permits-absent-package-runtime
assertions.description: Keeps package_manager null and runtime_version empty or null instead of inventing node, npm, or a runtime version

assertions.name: preserves-existing-container-path
assertions.description: Does not require known language metadata before preserving the existing Dockerfile path

assertions.name: continues-after-valid-analysis
assertions.description: Validates analysis.json and advances to Phase 1.5 rather than stopping the deployment in Phase 1

evals.prompt: Run Phase 6.5 against a healthy Next.js application whose initial HTTP response contains the internal NEXT_REDIRECT marker and redirects the browser to /project. Browser rendering, API checks, logs, and stability checks all pass.
evals.expected_output: The runtime truth pass treats NEXT_REDIRECT as a framework control-flow marker rather than a runtime failure, keeps the HTTP smoke result successful, and accepts the deployment based on the actual browser, HTTP status, logs, and stability evidence

assertions.name: ignores-normal-next-control-flow
assertions.description: Does not classify NEXT_REDIRECT alone as a smoke failure

assertions.name: retains-real-error-detection
assertions.description: Continues to fail on user-visible SSR error text and unsuccessful HTTP status codes

assertions.name: uses-runtime-evidence
assertions.description: Bases final acceptance on rendered browser behavior, HTTP status, logs, and stability rather than an internal framework digest
